variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
int a = 10;
auto b = 20; // Type inferred as int
immutable c = 30; // Cannot be changed
const d = 40; // Read-only view
variables.notes: D supports explicit typing, type inference with `auto`, and distinguishing between `const` (read-only) and `immutable` (guaranteed never to change).

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Strings in D are simply immutable arrays of UTF-8 characters (`immutable(char)[]`).

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: D includes unique operators like `^^` for exponentiation and `~` for array concatenation.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Conditionals are similar to C and C++, supporting standard `if/else` and ternary operators.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: The `foreach` loop is the idiomatic way to iterate, supporting ranges with `..`.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: Standard `while` and `do-while` loops are supported just like in C.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions can be marked `pure` or `nothrow`. D has incredibly powerful and concise template syntax.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
int[3] staticArr = [1, 2, 3]; // Fixed size
int[] dynamicArr = [1, 2, 3]; // Dynamic slice
dynamicArr ~= 4; // Append

int[] slice = dynamicArr[1..3];
arrays.notes: D features first-class built-in dynamic arrays (slices) and array operations, including vector math like `arr[] += 5`.

maps.title: Maps
maps.notes: Maps (associative arrays) are a built-in language feature in D, typed as `Value[Key]`.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: D uses standard exception handling. It also features `scope(exit)` and `scope(failure)` blocks for clean resource management.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: D uses C-style // single-line and /* */ multi-line comments.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: D provides explicitly sized integer and floating-point primitives with binary and hex support.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: D uses bool / boolean types with true and false literals and logical operators (&&, ||, !).

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.notes: D supports explicit type casting using cast operators or constructor functions.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.notes: D distinguishes between single-character literals and string sequences or pointer slices.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: D supports string interpolation or printf-style formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Switch
pattern_matching.notes: D evaluates branching conditions through switch statements, match expressions, or when constructs.

range.title: Ranges & Slicing
range.notes: D represents ranges with range operators (.., ..<) or standard indexed iteration boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Sequences
iterators.notes: D implements iteration through Iterator interfaces, generators, or range-for loops.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.notes: D models object orientation through classes with constructors/encapsulation or structs with associated methods.

lists.title: Dynamic Arrays & Lists
lists.notes: D manages growable dynamic collections using vectors, ArrayLists, or dynamically reallocated heap buffers.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: D represents heterogeneous records through tuples, structured bindings, or lightweight record structs.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Collections
sets.notes: D provides unique collection hashing structures with O(1) average lookup and insertion time.

modules_import.title: Modules, Packages & Imports
modules_import.notes: D structures namespaces and external libraries via include directives, package declarations, or module imports.
